<description>
Use CoinsViewOverlay to speed up ConnectBlock in TestBlockValidity. This also has the benefit of not inserting entries fetched from db into the main cache.

cs_main must be held for each place where the overlay is being used, and the reset guard ensures it will be reset for the next caller.
</description>

`TestBlockValidity()` previously used a local cache. This PR changes it to reuse `ConnectBlockView()`, which a synchronous `BlockChecked` callback can reach while `ConnectTip()` still has a fetch active.

Could we first record that both paths now select the same overlay?

```C++
BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(testblockvalidity_with_active_connect_view)
{
    auto tip_hash{WITH_LOCK(cs_main, return Assert(m_node.chainman)->ActiveTip()->GetBlockHash())};
    auto outer_block{BadBlock(tip_hash)};
    auto candidate_block{GoodBlock(tip_hash)};
    LOCK(cs_main);
    auto& chainstate{Assert(m_node.chainman)->ActiveChainstate()};
    auto reset_guard{chainstate.ConnectBlockView().StartFetching(*outer_block)};
    BOOST_CHECK(&chainstate.TestBlockValidityView() != &chainstate.ConnectBlockView());
    BOOST_CHECK(TestBlockValidity(chainstate, *candidate_block, /*check_pow=*/false, /*check_merkle_root=*/false).IsValid());
}
```

I don't think there is a reentrancy issue? I see though that `BlockChecked` callbacks in `ConnectTip` are synchronous, so a future change could theoretically call `TestBlockValidity` from the callback on the same thread. Nothing does that today. We can prevent this by calling `Assert(overlay_view.GetCacheSize() == 0);` inside `TestBlockValidity`. I'm not sure I see the value of this unit test.

@sedited thanks for the ping. I have been distracted by other issues but I am still interested in pursuing this. I will address @l0rinc's latest comments soon.

One thing I would like to understand better is how `checkBlock()` is used in practice. How often do we actually call it? One thing to consider is that with this method none of the uncached coins will be pre-emptively inserted into the cache. When many of the block's coins are not cached, this will be much faster on the first call. However, currently these coins will all be cached, while after this change they will not be. So subsequent calls with a similar block might be slower due to not inserting the coins in the cache.

@Sjors' idea https://github.com/Sjors/bitcoin/pull/122 might help here as well, but it's a much larger change.
